question_text: According to the course material, the final accounts of a sole trader consist of statement of profit or loss and statement of financial position; the statement of profit or loss for traders who deal in buying and selling typically reveals gross profit and:
explanation: Sole trader finals: profit or loss (and financial position).

question_text: According to the course material, expenses such as salaries are charged against the profit in the statement of profit or loss; when preparing that statement it should be done in a way to reveal the results of trading, and a typical statement of profit or loss is presented as:
explanation: Expenses charged against profit; format given as a guide.

question_text: According to the course material, the statement of financial position shows assets, liabilities and capital; it differs from the statement of profit or loss, which reports performance for a period, whereas the financial position is at:
explanation: Position at a date vs performance for a period.

question_text: According to the course material, end of year adjustments include prepayments, accruals, provisions and reserves; the amount owing on expenses is added to that expense in the statement of profit or loss and the unpaid amount is a liability, that is an:
explanation: Accrual: expense incurred but not yet paid.

question_text: According to the course material, a prepayment is recorded under current assets in the statement of financial position; the expense in the statement of profit or loss is the amount that relates to the period, after removing:
explanation: Prepaid expense = current asset; P&L gets the period's expense.

question_text: According to the course material, control accounts serve as the total or summary of what happens within a period; the control account under normal circumstance must equal the addition of individual customers or suppliers accounts; two major types are sales ledger (debtors) control and:
option_a: purchases ledger control or creditors control account
explanation: Debtors control and creditors control.

question_text: According to the course material, debtors control account is not used for cash customers; items that increase debts are debited to the debtors control account while those that will reduce the debts are:
explanation: Debtors control: debit increases, credit reductions. Cash customers excluded.

question_text: According to the course material, bills receivable discounted has nothing to do with the control account because the company has already received value; due to mistakes the control account may not agree with the addition of all the individual accounts and then investigation is:
explanation: Control vs listing differences must be investigated.

question_text: According to the course material, merits of control accounts include locating errors, acting as a check, providing total debtors and creditors quickly, and helping in internal control; they summarise many personal accounts into:
explanation: Control accounts summarise personal ledgers.

question_text: According to the course material, a bank reconciliation statement explains differences between the cash book bank balance and the bank statement; typical timing differences include unpresented cheques and:
explanation: Unpresented cheques and uncredited lodgements are classic reconciling items.

question_text: According to the course material, the course objectives include being able to prepare the statement of profit or loss of a sole trader, the statement of financial position of a sole trader, explain types of errors and how they are corrected, and prepare:
explanation: Objectives list bank reconciliation among the skills.

question_text: According to the course material, TMAs at the end of each unit are designed to test understanding; besides preparatory TMAs, examinable TMAs marked electronically make up to 30 percent of the total score for the course, with the rest typically the:
explanation: Examinable TMAs = 30% of the course score.

explanation: Units 17-18 are the two sole-trader final-account units.

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 19 treats end of year adjustments in final accounts, for example prepayment, accruals, provisions and reserves; matching concept brought about these adjustments so profit or loss for the period can be:
explanation: Year-end adjustments implement matching.

question_text: According to the course material, Head of Department for the ACC203 material is Dr Ofe Inua, Department of Financial Studies, National Open University of Nigeria, and the programme coordinator is:

question_text: According to the course material, opening stock plus purchases less closing stock relates to cost of goods sold in the trading section of the statement of profit or loss; closing stock is also shown as a current asset in:
explanation: Closing stock in both COGS and current assets.

question_text: According to the course material, drawings are withdrawals by the owner and reduce capital; they are not business expenses and should not be charged in the statement of profit or loss but deducted from:
option_a: capital in the statement of financial position
explanation: Drawings: reduce capital, not an expense.

question_text: According to the course material, a provision is an end-of-year adjustment example listed with prepayments, accruals and reserves; the course content focuses on treatment of accounting transactions according to the provisions of relevant:
explanation: Content: treatment according to relevant accounting standards.

question_text: According to the course material, sales ledger control records the total of each transaction as it affects all the customers for the month; the balance on the control account should be equal to the addition of the individual:
explanation: Debtors control = sum of individual debtors.

question_text: According to the course material, creditors control is credited with transactions that increase amounts owed to suppliers and debited with those that reduce the debt to suppliers; it is also called:
explanation: Purchases ledger control = creditors control.

question_text: According to the course material, bank reconciliation is Unit 21, the last unit; the course aim includes practical treatment of accounting transactions conducted through the bank so that the cash book can be agreed to:
explanation: Bank rec agrees cash book to bank statement.

question_text: According to the course material, the course material consists of both academic and professional materials, providing the opportunity of obtaining a BSc. degree in Accounting and preparation for:
explanation: Academic plus professional exam preparation.

question_text: According to the course material, self-assessment exercises in each unit should be attempted as this will enable you understand the content of the unit; TMAs test understanding and application of the concepts learned and some are marked:
explanation: SAQs plus electronically marked TMAs.

question_text: According to the course material, control accounts may not agree with the schedule of debtors because of mistakes in the control account and/or individual customers' accounts; an audit may reveal errors such as an account in the purchase ledger that had not been entered in:
explanation: Listing vs control differences from omitted personal accounts.
